text: dsh-image-base64 是一个用于 DSH 的图像格式兼容插件。它在 attachments 服务就绪后包装 readImageRequest()，让视觉模型请求取得图像时检查媒体类型。默认保留 PNG、JPEG 和 GIF；其他格式使用 sharp 转码为 PNG，并返回更新后的图像数据和媒体类型。适合经由严格校验图像 MIME 类型的兼容网关发送视觉请求的场景。可通过 acceptedMediaTypes 配置直接放行的格式，使用时需要 DSH attachments 服务和 sharp。

dsh-image-base64 is a DSH image compatibility plugin. It checks media types before vision requests: PNG, JPEG, and GIF pass through by default; other formats are converted to PNG with sharp. Configure acceptedMediaTypes for a different pass-through list.
DSH 的视觉请求遇到 WebP 格式不兼容时，能自动转成 PNG 吗？
想让发给模型的图片符合网关接受的 MIME 类型。
图片请求被兼容接口拒绝，因为图像编码格式不受支持，怎么处理？
让 DSH 在请求视觉模型前把不支持的图像格式转为 PNG。
Can DSH convert unsupported image formats to PNG before a vision request?
My OpenAI-compatible gateway rejects WebP image data; how can I make DSH send PNG instead?
能不能让不支持的图片媒体类型在发送前自动转成兼容格式？
有什么办法让透明截图也能用于视觉模型请求？
dsh-image-base64 的功能「请求图像格式兼容」：读取模型请求所需的图像后，检查其媒体类型；默认让 PNG、JPEG、GIF 原样通过，其他类型用 sharp 转码为 PNG，再返回新的图像数据和 MIME 类型。
dsh-image-base64 的功能「可配置的放行格式」：通过 acceptedMediaTypes 设置哪些媒体类型无需转码，默认值为 image/png、image/jpeg 和 image/gif；未列出的类型会被转换为 PNG。
dsh-image-base64 的功能「补丁生命周期恢复」：插件 effect 安装对 readImageRequest() 的包装，并在清理时仅当当前方法仍是自身包装时恢复原方法。

dsh-image-base64 README · dsh-image-base64：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that fixes:

```
This turn failed 400 "'url' field must be a base64 encoded image."
INVALID_REQUEST
```

when a vision-capable model (e.g. `meta/muse-glimmer`) is served through an
OpenAI-compatible gateway that validates the image MIME type strictly, such
as **LM Studio**.

dsh-image-base64 README · Why this happens：See [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness#4615](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4615)
for the full discussion. The short version:

dsh-image-base64 README · Why this happens：- `dsh-attachment-local`'s request-image quality ladder re-encodes an image
  as `image/webp` whenever the source has an alpha channel (JPEG has no
  alpha channel to fall back to). A pasted screenshot or a PNG with
  transparency very often has one.
- LM Studio's OpenAI-compatible endpoint only accepts `image/png`,
  `image/jpeg`, and `image/gif` inside a base64 `data:` URL. It rejects
  `image/webp` (and anything else) at the protocol layer with `400`, before
  the request reaches the model.
- `dsh-llm-pi-ai` forwards whatever `mediaType` the attachment store gives
  it straight into the request — there's no format negotiation between the
  two, so the mismatch reaches LM Studio unchanged.

dsh-image-base64 README · What this plugin does：It wraps the attachment store's `readImageRequest()` (the call
`dsh-llm-pi-ai` makes to get the exact bytes/MIME type that go into the
request) and transcodes the result to `image/png` with `sharp` whenever its
media type isn't in an accepted list (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`
by default). Everything already in an accepted format passes through
untouched — only the images that would otherwise be rejected pay the
transcode cost.

dsh-image-base64 README · Install：From your DSH profile directory (or via `dsh plugin --profile <name> add`,
which forwards to `pnpm` inside the profile):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /home/pakkapon/dsh-image-base64
```

Then list it in that profile's `package.json` under `dsh.profile.bundles`:

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [

Restart the profile (or let it pick it up automatically if
`patchReload: live` is set) to load it.

dsh-image-base64 README · Configuration：Accepted media types default to `[image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif]` (LM
Studio's whitelist). To widen or narrow that, target the plugin's `id` from
your own patch layer (profile `cordis.patch.yml` or `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: image-base64-compat
  config:
    acceptedMediaTypes: [image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp]
```

dsh-image-base64 README · Caveats：- This patches the attachment store's *request-image* projection only — it
  doesn't touch how images are stored, just what's sent on the wire for a
  model request.
- Transcoding to PNG is lossless for the pixels it's given, but a PNG
  re-encode of a large photo is bigger than an equivalent JPEG/WebP. If your
  gateway actually accepts WebP, add it to `acceptedMediaTypes` instead of
  relying on the default.
